title: Linear differential operators, superposition, and solution spaces
section: Higher-Order Linear Equations with Constant Coefficients ▷ Linear structure and general solutions

question.text:
Functions u, v satisfy L[u] = f and L[v] = 2f, where L is a linear differential operator and
f ̸≡ 0. Which is necessarily a homogeneous solution?
2
(A) u + v (B) 2u − v (C) uv (D) u − v (E) u − v

solution.text:
Linearity gives L[2u − v] = 2f − 2f = 0. No product rule or square rule implies analogous
cancellation for the nonlinear expressions. The other linear combinations give nonzero
multiples of f.

Expanding the first equation gives e y + x y + 2xy = 0: every appearance of the unknown

independent variable in a linear equation.

On each side of zero, separation gives y = C x for x < 0 and y = C x for x > 0.

The equation at zero requires y(0) = 0, and any two constants give matching value and
first derivative zero there. Thus the space has two independent parameters. The usual
dimension-equals-order theorem does not apply across a zero of the leading coefficient.
